subject: Q1 2026 Cost Allocation Report - DataLytics Subscription
body:
# Q1 2026 Internal Cost Allocation Report
**Subject**: DataLytics Cloud Subscription Expense Attribution
**Date**: March 30, 2026
**Prepared by**: Wei Chenghao / Chenghao Studio
**Purpose**: Tax filing documentation (Q1 2026 individual business income)

---

## Executive Summary
DataLytics Cloud subscription was upgraded mid-month (March 15) due to API rate limits triggered by client feature usage. Total Q1 expense: ¥2,640. Billable portion: ¥600. Net absorbed cost: ¥2,040.

## Expense Breakdown

### January 2026
- Service: DataLytics Cloud API (Standard tier)
- Amount: ¥680
- Usage: ~6.5k API calls/day average
- Attribution: General business expense (multiple clients)

### February 2026
- Service: DataLytics Cloud API (Standard tier)
- Amount: ¥680
- Usage: ~7.2k API calls/day average
- Attribution: General business expense

### March 2026
- Service: DataLytics Cloud API (Standard → Pro tier)
- Base charge (Mar 1-14): ¥680
- Upgrade charge (Mar 15-31): ¥600 prorated
- **Total**: ¥1,280
- Usage: 8.5k calls/day → spike to 14.8k calls/day (Mar 13-14)
- **Trigger**: TechSolutions/Li Qiang batch export feature

## Client Attribution Analysis

**Client**: Li Qiang / TechSolutions Co.
**Contract**: SaaS Platform Maintenance Agreement (2025-10-01 ~ 2026-09-30)
**Feature Request**: Batch report export (requested Feb 20, deployed Mar 5)
**Usage Pattern**: 15-20 export jobs/day during testing phase (Mar 12-14)
**API Impact**: Each export = ~200 API calls → 3,000-4,000 additional calls/day

### Contract Review (Section 4.3)
> "If client feature requests or usage patterns require upgrade of third-party API service tiers (e.g., DataLytics, payment gateways), such upgrade costs are billable to client on a prorated basis from upgrade date."

**Billability Decision**: ✅ BILLABLE
- Upgrade directly caused by client-requested feature
- Usage spike clearly attributable to single client
- Contract explicitly permits API tier upgrade billing
- Client notification sent March 30 (7-day advance notice per contract)

## Financial Impact

### Q1 2026 Expense Summary
- Gross DataLytics expense: ¥2,640
- Less: Billable to TechSolutions: (¥600)
- **Net absorbed cost**: ¥2,040

### Profit Margin Impact
- Q1 revenue: ¥95,200
- Q1 total expenses: ¥4,537 (including net DataLytics cost)
- Gross profit: ¥90,663
- Margin: 95.2%

## Action Items Completed
- [x] Verified upgrade trigger in project logs (Obsidian: OBSN-38)
- [x] Reviewed contract billability terms (Obsidian: OBSN-39)
- [x] Calculated cost delta and proration
- [x] Drafted client notification (Fossify Notes: FNOT-231)
- [x] Documented decision for tax filing
- [x] Sent this report to personal email for records

## Supporting Documentation
- Transaction records: My Expenses GUI (MYEXP-001, MYEXP-002, MYEXP-004)
- Finance system: TXN-6021, TXN-6022, TXN-6023
- Project analysis: Obsidian OBSN-38 (API usage timeline)
- Contract terms: Obsidian OBSN-39 (Section 4.3)
- Client communication: Fossify Notes FNOT-231 (notification draft)

## Tax Filing Notes
- Individual business income (个体工商户)
- Q1 filing deadline: April 15, 2026
- Net business expense properly documented
- Billable amount will appear as revenue offset in Q2 (April invoice)

---

**Report Status**: Final
**Next Review**: Q2 2026 (June 30)

*This report is for internal accounting and tax preparation purposes. Retain for audit trail.*

subject: Indie Dev Weekly #148: Managing API Costs in Client Projects
body:
Hi Wei,

Welcome to Indie Dev Weekly #148!

This week's theme: **Managing API costs when building for clients**

## Featured Article
**When to Bill Back Infrastructure Costs**
Many indie devs absorb all infrastructure costs to keep client relationships simple. But as your projects scale, this can eat into margins. Here's a framework:

1. **Always billable**: Costs triggered by client-specific features
2. **Usually billable**: Tier upgrades due to client usage spikes
3. **Rarely billable**: General infrastructure improvements

Key: Document the attribution clearly and reference contract terms.

## Tools of the Week
- **API Usage Tracker**: Set alerts before hitting tier limits
- **Cost Attribution Templates**: Track which client triggered what upgrade

## Community Spotlight
Developer @chenghao shared: "Just caught a DataLytics tier upgrade before it hit my invoice. Turns out a client's batch export feature was the culprit. Contract let me bill it back - saved ¥600/month!"

Great example of proactive cost management!

Happy building,
The Indie Dev Weekly Team
